Hi all — thanks for looping me in, and hello Dana. We're happy to support Metro Parks on this. Below is a concise package and our position summary.

Attachments (initial packet):
- Redwood_SIG_partial.xlsx (workbook) — Completed SIG Lite export; a few vendor-specific items are marked 'in progress' where we map to partner controls.
- SOC2-2025-report.pdf (application/pdf) — Redacted SOC 2 Type II (Dec 2025) report.
- DPIA-exec-summary.docx (application/msword) — High-level data flow and retention summary for public-sector use cases.
- SCCs-execution-stmt.pdf (application/pdf) — Our standard SCCs execution statement and process notes.

Summary / responses to your bullets:
1) SIG/CAIQ: our SIG Lite workbook is attached. We can also provide a completed CAIQ on request but the SIG output covers the required procurement fields for Metro Parks.

2) SOC 2: redacted copy attached. If procurement requires an auditor letter, we can coordinate a notarized attestation.

3) SCCs / DPA: Redwood will sign a controller-to-processor Data Processing Addendum that incorporates the EU SCCs (2021 standard clauses). For the state privacy annex: we typically accept procurement addenda provided they do not modify core security or retention obligations (we will flag any clauses that attempt to shift processor obligations to Redwood in a way that is inconsistent with our standard DPA). If you can share the exact annex language, we will propose minimal redlines within 48 hours.

4) DPIA: Attached is a 1–2 page executive DPIA summary describing data categories (public park visitors, scheduling/registration info, limited PII such as name/email), flow diagrams at a high level, and standard retention baselines (default 90 days for request logs, 1 year for registration records unless contract specifies otherwise). If Metro Parks needs a deeper DPIA we can supply a template and a scoped statement of work.

5) FedRAMP-adjacent controls: we maintain an internal controls mapping to NIST SP 800-53 and SOC 2 criteria; we can produce a short alignment table showing how key RFP controls map to our program. We are not FedRAMP certified; procurement should treat items labeled 'FedRAMP-adjacent' as guidance only.

Proposed next steps:
- We will send the complete packet after the call and provide redline suggestions on any annex that procurement shares.
- If procurement requires a signed SCCs execution statement prior to execution of the master services agreement, we can provide the SCCs-execution-stmt.pdf for signature.

Call: Wed 05 Aug 10:00–10:30 ET — sending invite now.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Privacy & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
